item.description: muirbhuachaill, great northern diver. (Tarbert)
àite còmhnaidh, taigh, togail, bothan. Am fuireachan àite sin shìos.
aodach sracte, luidean. Sc. dudds, duddies.
beagan sgadain sgapte. A strawing. Sràbhail bheag sgadain ris a’ chladach.
àrd amach, fada amach anns a’ mhuir.
extravagant. (Ìle) Tha e ròramach (ròromach) le cuid dhaoine eile. < ro + rùm?
peasanta, peasanach. (Tarbert)
big and imposing. Tha i dàicheil gu leòir air son a’ ghunna: she’s big and imposing enough to shoulder a rifle.
trim. Dé’n gleus a th’ort = Dé’n trim a th’ort?
a slipper. > Sc. bauchle? Sean bhachall bàta.
a fisherman’s neck scarf. Gràbhat beag lìn.
herring scales on the sides and deck of a boat (giving an impression of reodhadh). Fhuair iad sgadan – tha reòtach oirre.
stonechats assembling on the rocks on the shore in the autumn are called this.
a grapnel.
barra-cuibhle. (Tarbert)
adhar beag gaoithe – a waft.

item.headword: Letter and word-list dated 06/05/1976: Air son an fhaclair

item.description: “Tha mi’n dòchas gu’m bi am beagan beag fhacal a tha mi ’cur gu’d ionnsaigh a chum feuma. Tha corra fhacal agam o Chinntàile. ’S e Tàileach d’am b’ainm Crìsdein MacRath a bu phrìomh charaid dhomh nuair a bha mi ’san oilthigh.”
(Mur eil ainm ceàrnaidh no dùthcha ’ga thoirt seachad is ann o’n Tairbeart Loch Fìne a thà na facail seo.)
a roch [sic] cod.
a large crab.
a clam.
dad, càil. Cha d’fhuair mi gas.
herring split and laid out to dry on a rock in the sun. Roc An Sgadain-Ghréin’: an underwater rock. The markings on it resemble split herring.
shoot (a met [sic] [net?]). An do chuir sibh, ’fheara? Iomair mu thuath agus cuir mu dheas (proverb): Row north and shoot south.
Tha cur an tsneachda [sic] trom. (Islay)
punning slang for a tumbler to drink out of.
a kind of shellfish.
[See claba-dubh.]
a squid. (‘Ink fish’ in the dialect of the East Coast.) If I remember, this word occurs in MacPhaidein.
a gannet, solan goose, solan.
[kɛ:rsɑN] the hoarse sound of rising sea and wind. Tha càrsan beag ann anochd.
a hump back.
humpbacked.
a snipe.
slang for hand – ‘mitt’. Bheil do mhòganan fuar? Are your mitts cold?
a Medusa, kind of jellyfish. < O.N. skjöldur, skjöld; a shield?
slang for a foot. Tha mi ’dol a shìneadh mo spàgan: I’m going for a walk.
poles on the shore for drying nets. Cuiridh sinn an lìon air a’ chroich. (They have all disappeared.) ‘Crochans’ in English.
[sic] an angler fish.
a net rope (ring net).
the planking at the stern.
bigmouthed, boastful, a blow. Ràiteach occurs in Dwelly, I think.
‘appearance’ in English. Signs of herring. Cha n-eil coltas ann idir. This word occurs in MacPhaidein (A’ ruith nan coltas feadh nan cuantan).
phosphorescence. (Burning, the burning in Tarbert English.) This reveals the presence of herring at night, hence ‘Gheobh sinn iad ’san losgadh.’
an extension of the meaning ‘clump’. A small clump of herring. Tha toman dhiubh fodhainn.
of a blind or shortsighted man – Cha n-fhaic e leus.
of a deaf man – Cha chluinn e deò.
a hare.
Walter. Uaimh Bhaltair, Rudha Bhaltair, Pàra Bhaltair.
a fish weir. There are the remains of one in a level bay north of Tarbert.
a gorge of food. Ghabhainn glàm dhiubh sin.
a white-throated diver.
calm. Ma bhìos e fèathail mochthrath.
punctilious, exact, careful of one’s appearance.
gille.
a gurnet. A man’s nickname.
Mochrath [sic] maith dhuit = madainn mhaith dhuit. Thà mi dol a chur mo cheann far am faigh mi e mochthrath.
(with the accent on the second syllable) (ro + ? ?) overbearing behaviour. (Kintail)
violent, overbearing behaviour. (Kintail)
a tivking [sic] [ticking?] off. (Kintail)
an eye-opener. (Kintail – in Dwelly)
a garden. (Kintail) Nuair a bha mi ag obair anns an lios ud thall.
(< -chriothach?) a quagmire. Sùil-chrith in Islay, I was told a long time ago.
a buoy. Equally a sea-mark or a buoy on a net.
Notes: ‘smirr, drizzle, small rain’. Tarbert Argyll and Islay usage. ‘Baile na Smùrach’ used as fisherman’s slang for Ardrossan (‘dross’).
Quotation: uair mhath. Notes: ‘good weather’. Tarbert and Islay usage.
